# Methods
Our research question is if the patal width correlates with petal length. we have to columns of continuos data which measures in millimeters. we will use simple correlation analysis and also scatter plot, tehse 2 methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like this.


# Results
using the classical simple pearson correalation we approch these data.there is a very positive correlation between the width and length of paddel of flowers (.96).
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')
print(df.sample(3))
# Correlation between petal length and petal width
r = df['petal_length'].corr(df['petal_width'])
print(f"Correlation (r) between petal length and petal width: {r:.2f}")

# Scatterplot
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='petal_length', y='petal_width')

#heatmap
sns.heatmap(df.groupby('species').mean(), annot=True, cmap='YlGnBu')
plt.title("Average Measurements by Species")
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from itertools import combinations

sns.set_theme(style="white")
df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

# All 6 pairs of the 4 measurements
pairs = list(combinations(['sepal_length', 'sepal_width',
                           'petal_length', 'petal_width'], 2))

# Set up the matplotlib figure
f, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(12, 8))

# Rotate the starting point around the cubehelix hue circle
for ax, (x_col, y_col), s in zip(axes.flat, pairs, np.linspace(0, 3, 6)):

    # Create a cubehelix colormap to use with kdeplot
    cmap = sns.cubehelix_palette(start=s, light=1, as_cmap=True)

    # Plot the density of this pair of measurements
    sns.kdeplot(
        data=df, x=x_col, y=y_col,
        cmap=cmap, fill=True,
        thresh=0, levels=15,
        ax=ax,
    )
    ax.set_title(f"{x_col} vs. {y_col}")

f.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
